title: Having Split
statement: Implement `solve(clauses)`. Each clause is `[text, kind]` where kind is `row` or `agg`. Return `{"where": [...], "having": [...]}` with the texts. Row filters go to where. Aggregate filters go to having. Order is preserved.
constraints: Do not look at the text to guess

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: WHERE runs before grouping and cannot see aggregates.

editorial: WHERE runs before grouping and cannot see aggregates. HAVING runs after. Putting a customer filter in HAVING is legal in some engines and wasteful. Putting COUNT in WHERE is an error. The kind flag is the writer's decision, and the split is where the SQL clauses go.
